facts.fact: Approximately 6 billion people, 74% of the global population, used the internet in 2025, according to the ITU's Facts and Figures 2025 as cited by the vendor.

facts.fact: The W3C began work on mobile-web guidance in 2005, according to the W3C history of mobile best practices cited by the vendor.

facts.fact: The W3C Mobile Web Best Practices 1.0 became an official Recommendation on July 29, 2008.

facts.fact: The W3C Mobile Web Best Practices 1.0 contained 60 best practices, and roughly half could be traced to accessibility guidance.

facts.fact: Google moved most sites to smartphone-based crawling and made mobile-first indexing the default for new sites.
facts.quote: Google moved most sites to smartphone-based crawling and made mobile-first indexing the default for new sites.

facts.fact: The W3C mobile accessibility mapping guidance recommends a minimum touch target size of 9 mm by 9 mm.
facts.quote: designing touch controls with a **minimum target size of 9 mm by 9 mm**

facts.fact: The W3C mobile accessibility mapping guidance recommends placing form fields below their labels in portrait orientation.
facts.quote: placing form fields below their labels in portrait orientation

facts.fact: Google's mobile speed guidance for advertisers reports that in retail, each additional second of page-load delay can reduce conversions by up to 20%.
facts.quote: each additional second of page-load delay can reduce conversions by up to 20%

facts.fact: Google's mobile speed guidance recommends evaluating whether a page can render in under one second on a mobile network.
facts.quote: evaluating whether a page can render in under one second on a mobile network

facts.fact: Google's broader guidance cites five seconds or less as a practical target for 3G conditions.
facts.quote: its broader guidance cites five seconds or less as a practical target for 3G conditions

facts.fact: The page's phone-width layout standard calls for building the 320 to 390 pixel layout first.

facts.fact: Google uses the mobile version of a webpage's content, crawled with a smartphone user agent, for indexing and ranking, according to Google's mobile-first indexing guidance as cited on the page.
facts.quote: Google uses the mobile version of a webpage’s content, crawled with a smartphone user agent, for indexing and ranking

facts.fact: Google warns that content present only on desktop may not be used for Search indexing or ranking.
